I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize cycle because that is the most familiar and dependable way I farm, and I have well irrigation so I can support both crops through dry spells. I will leave a smaller part of the land for peanut because it brings useful cash income and spreads my risk. Since my family has some off-farm work, I will choose inputs and field operations that are steady and manageable rather than overly intensive. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give enough base fertilizer and a couple of irrigations, and aim for a stable yield. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on the same land because it yields well and fits my usual system. For peanut, I will keep fertilizer moderate, use fewer irrigations than wheat, and manage pests carefully but not excessively. I will use rotary tillage because it saves labor and fits the way I would handle 7 mu at the start of the season.
